jobs.title: Director Threat Intelligence
jobs.description:
Job Description

Location: Winnipeg, Toronto

Referral Level: Level 1

Mackenzie Investments

IGM Financial Inc. is a leading wealth and asset management company in Canada, managing approximately $ 310 billion in assets as of December 31, 2025 . It offers financial planning and investment services to over two million Canadians through IG Wealth Management and Mackenzie Investments.

Mackenzie Investments, founded in 1967, is a key part of IGM's business model, serving as a comprehensive asset-management partner for Canadian financial advisors and their clients.

At Mackenzie Investments You Can Build Your Career with Confidence.
We are proud to be recognized as one of Canada’s Top 100 Employers for the fourth consecutive year and one of Canada’s Best Diversity Employers. Our vision and strategy aim to innovate the industry and support Canadians in achieving their financial goals.

Join our team to engage in continuous learning and skill development in a supportive environment. Experience the best of both worlds with our hybrid work environment, where you spend three days a week in the office, connecting, collaborating, and enjoying quality time with your amazing colleagues ! Our Values: Be better ; we strive for improvement in everything we do . Be accountable ; we foster clarity and are empowered to act responsibly . Be a team ; we are united to drive collective impact to achieve our goals .

Overall Job Purpose

Accountable for enterprise strategy, standards, and guardrails across security platform and infrastructure engineering, with a direct mandate to mature Threat Intelligence and DevSecOps as day to day operating capabilities. Shapes policy enforcement, resolves systemic constraints across multiple teams, and influences senior stakeholders on investment, resilience, and risk trade-offs, translating enterprise considerations into actionable governance aligned to Technology standards.

Key Accountabilities

Enterprise Strategy, Standards, and Guardrails
Define and evolve enterprise platform and infrastructure standards spanning tooling, pipelines, shared services, automation, resilience, recoverability, and observability, and drive adoption across portfolios.
Serve as trusted advisor on the highest-complexity platform, infrastructure, and operational resilience issues across multiple teams.
Threat Intelligence Enablement
Own the enterprise standards for threat intelligence collection, enrichment, and dissemination so that intel drives compensating control recommendations for operators.
Translate threat intelligence into prioritized, evidence-based guardrails and detection requirements across the security ecosystem.
DevSecOps and Secure Delivery
Sponsor policy-as-code, automation, and knowledge automation practices so security controls are codified, machine-testable, and enforced within pipelines.
Define safe automation and CI/CD enablement patterns that embed security guardrails into build, test, deploy, and operate workflows.
Systemic Constraint Resolution
Resolve systemic platform and infrastructure constraints impacting delivery speed, reliability, security, capacity, stability, or recoverability across multiple teams.
Resilience, Incident, and Operational Readiness
Drive observability, resilience, and incident learning at enterprise scale, including telemetry, alerting, capacity, and DR readiness, to improve service maturity.
Influence, Investment, and Escalation Governance
Influence roadmap and investment decisions with evidence-based trade-offs on capability, risk, resilience, cost, and scalability.
Determine when initiatives require escalation due to enterprise or regulatory impact and ensure consistent engagement with architecture and risk forums.
Partner with senior stakeholders to align priorities and sequencing when constraints materially impact outcomes.
AI-Enabled Practices
Shape and sponsor AI-enabled platform and infrastructure strategy, including automation, predictive monitoring, and policy-as-code, aligned to security and governance.
People and Capability Uplift
Mentor senior ICs and strengthen capability uplift through communities of practice and standards forums.
Continuous Improvement
Identify recurring friction and enable durable fixes across the platform and infrastructure ecosystem.

Qualifications

Post-secondary education in Technology or related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Extensive progressive experience delivering enterprise platform and infrastructure services and enablement.
Proven influence on standards, governance alignment, and risk-informed decisions across multiple teams.
Demonstrated leadership-by-influence with senior stakeholders and governance forums.
Deep expertise in automation, CI/CD enablement, observability, recoverability, and secure operations.
Ability to shape AI-enabled strategy and guardrails at scale.
Demonstrated depth in Threat Intelligence and DevSecOps as core operating disciplines.

The expected annual base salary range for this role is $149,500 - $192,500
which is determined based on skills, knowledge and experience and geographic location. In addition to base salary, this role is eligible for annual short-term incentive, health and well-being benefits, retirement and savings plan, paid time off and career development.

Benefits

COMPETITIVE COMPENSATION & RECOGNITION: competitive base salary, performance-weighted bonus, education/career support, option to join Employee Share Purchase Plan with employer matching component.
EMPLOYEE BENEFITS & INSURANCE: competitive health and dental coverage, flexible plan for you and your family and short-term & long-term disability plans.
RETIREMENT SAVINGS PROGRAMS: voluntary Defined Contribution Pension Plan
WORK LIFE BALANCE: paid volunteer days, competitive time off, including 10 wellness days off, WorkPerks discount program, hybrid & flex work arrangements.
INCLUSIVE CULTURE AND DIVERSITY: living our core values: Be a Team, Be Accountable, Be Better, engaging with community through Business Resource Groups (BRG communities are volunteer employee-led groups formed around a common interest, identity, or background).

IGM is a diverse workplace committed to doing business inclusively - this starts with having a representative workforce! We encourage applications from all qualified candidates that represent the diversity present across Canada – including racialized persons, women, Indigenous persons, persons with disabilities, 2SLGBTQIA+ community, gender diverse and neurodiverse individuals, as well as all who may contribute to the further diversification of ideas.

Mackenzie Investments is an accessible employer committed to providing barrier -free recruitment experience. If you require accommodation or this information in an alternate format at any stage of the recruitment process, please reach out to the Talent Acquisition team who will work with you to meet your needs .

How to Apply:
Interested candidates are invited to submit their resume and a cover letter detailing their qualifications and experience to https://www.mackenzieinvestments.com/en/careers
.

Artificial Intelligence in Recruitment:
As part of our Talent Acquisition process, we may use artificial intelligence and automated tools to support activities such as candidate sourcing, application review, and interview scheduling. These tools support the recruitment process; all hiring decisions are made by people.

We thank all applicants for their interest in Mackenzie Investments; however, only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

CleanDesign is a Canadian cleantech company developing hybrid energy management systems that help industrial and infrastructure operators reduce fuel consumption, lower emissions, and improve power reliability. Its solutions combine battery storage, controls, embedded systems, and software to optimize energy usage in demanding operating environments where uptime and resiliency are critical. The company’s work spans applications across oil and gas, mining, EV charging, remote communities, and other critical infrastructure sectors.

Job Description

Build and maintain multi-scenario models across core and emerging product lines
Lead budgeting, forecasting, and internal planning processes
Evaluate new business verticals, product initiatives, and growth opportunities
Define and track KPIs and performance dashboards

Evaluate partnership and M&A opportunities
Financial modelling, valuation, and diligence for potential transactions
Support deal structuring, negotiations, and contract review
Monitor industry trends, competitor activities, and regulatory developments to
identify opportunities and risks

needs

relations

Lead ad-hoc strategic projects under tight timelines and ambiguity
Prepare executive-ready materials for leadership and board presentations

5+ years of working experience as a Financial Analyst

University degree in Finance, Accounting, Commerce, or Data Management

jobs.title: Director of Finance & Administration
jobs.description:
Director of Finance & Administration

Groundswell Food Group, Inc. (DBA Mitsoh)
Location: Remote
Reports to: Chief Executive Officer (CEO)
About Mitsoh

Mitsoh is building a new generation of clean-protein foods rooted in tradition and made for modern lifestyles. Our products are crafted with a focus on high-quality ingredients, nutritional integrity, and responsible sourcing. As a rapidly growing CPG food company, we operate with world-class manufacturing and food safety standards aligned with GFSI-recognized programs.

We are seeking a hands-on and strategic Director of Finance & Administration to build the financial infrastructure, controls, and administrative systems required to scale Mitsoh into a world-class food manufacturing company and consumer brand.

Position Overview

The Director of Finance & Administration is responsible for leading Mitsoh’s finance, accounting, and administrative functions, including financial reporting, planning and analysis, product costing, cash management, HR and payroll administration, and business systems.

Reporting to the CEO and leading a small team, this role partners closely with operations, supply chain, and commercial teams to drive margin visibility, cost discipline, and data-driven decision-making across both the manufacturing and brand sides of the business. This is a builder’s role — equally comfortable setting strategy with leadership and rolling up sleeves to close the month.

Key Responsibilities

Accounting & Financial Reporting

Own the full accounting cycle, including month-end close, reconciliations, and preparation of accurate, timely financial statements

Maintain the integrity of the general ledger, chart of accounts, and financial controls as the company scales

Manage accounts receivable, accounts payable, collections, and customer/vendor account reconciliation

Oversee inventory accounting, including raw materials, WIP, finished goods, and reconciliation of physical counts to system records

Manage external accountant, audit, and tax relationships, including year-end preparation and regulatory filings

Financial Planning & Analysis

Lead annual budgeting, rolling forecasts, and scenario planning aligned with company growth objectives

Deliver monthly reporting packages with variance analysis and plain-language commentary for leadership and the board

Build KPI dashboards and reporting across revenue, margin, cash, and operational performance

Provide financial modeling and analysis to support pricing, capital investment, and growth decisions

Product Costing & Margin Management

Own standard costing for manufactured products, including BOMs, yields, labor, and overhead absorption

Analyze cost variances between standard and actual production performance and drive corrective visibility

Deliver margin analysis by product, channel, and customer across DTC, retail, and distributor networks

Partner with operations and supply chain on COGS reduction, waste, and yield improvement initiatives

Revenue, Trade & Channel Finance

Manage revenue recognition and channel-specific billing across DTC, retail, and distributor accounts

Track and validate trade spend, promotions, chargebacks, and distributor deductions

Support commercial teams with customer profitability analysis and pricing guidance

Monitor and reconcile e-commerce platform payouts, fees, and settlements

Cash Management & Treasury

Own cash flow forecasting and working capital management, including inventory, receivables, and payables cycles

Manage banking relationships, credit facilities, and financing arrangements

Support capital raising, government funding programs, and grant applications as required

Ensure disciplined spend management and approval controls across the organization

HR & Payroll Administration

Administer payroll, group benefits, and related remittances and filings

Oversee employee onboarding, offboarding, records, and HR policy administration

Ensure compliance with employment standards and related regulatory requirements

Support leadership on compensation planning and people-related processes as the team grows

Business Systems & IT Administration

Own the company’s ERP and financial systems, ensuring data integrity and effective integration across order management, inventory, and accounting

Manage software subscriptions, IT vendors, and technology spend

Drive automation and process improvement across finance and administrative workflows

Support the selection and implementation of new systems as the company scales

Leadership & Team Development

Build, lead, and develop the finance and administration team

Establish clear processes, documentation, and cross-training across the function

Serve as a trusted business partner to the CEO and leadership team

Foster a culture of accountability, accuracy, and continuous improvement

Qualifications

CPA designation required

8–10+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including leadership roles within a CPG food or beverage manufacturing environment

Strong experience with product costing, inventory accounting, and manufacturing finance

Experience across DTC, retail, and distributor channels, including trade spend and deduction management

Proven track record leading budgeting, forecasting, and financial reporting for a growing company

Experience administering payroll, benefits, and HR processes in a small-to-mid-size company

Strong ERP and systems experience, including implementations or integrations

Advanced financial modeling and analytical skills

Core Competencies

Financial leadership and business partnership

Manufacturing costing and margin management

Planning, forecasting, and analysis

Cash and working capital management

Controls, compliance, and accuracy

Systems and process improvement

Team building and development

Clear communication with financial and non-financial audiences

Additional Information

This is a remote role. Periodic travel to Mitsoh’s Leduc, Alberta facility and operational partners may be required for planning cycles, inventory counts, and leadership meetings.

What We’re Looking For

Mitsoh is looking for a builder. The ideal candidate is technically strong, highly operational, and energized by creating financial and administrative infrastructure from the ground up. This leader will bring the discipline, visibility, and systems required to scale a modern food company — while staying hands-on in a lean, fast-moving environment.

jobs.title: Senior IT Auditor, VP Finance
jobs.description:
Description

University Audit Services
in VP Finance
is currently seeking a Full-time Regular Senior IT Auditor
.

Reporting to the IT Audit Manager, the Senior IT Auditor plays a key role in delivering the University's technology audit program. This position is responsible for executing and leading IT audit engagements and providing independent, objective assurance over the effectiveness of IT processes and controls.

Operating within a complex and decentralized academic environment, the Senior IT Auditor will work closely with business and IT stakeholders to identify risks and practical improvements that support organizational objectives. The successful candidate combines strong technical knowledge with business acumen to evaluate both technology and business risks, provide advisory services, and contribute to the continuous improvement of the organization's control environment.

Summary of Key Responsibilities
(job functions include but are not limited to):

Technology Audit Delivery (Primary Focus)

Lead and execute complex IT assurance engagements, from planning through reporting.
Identify and assess risks related to cybersecurity, privacy, business continuity, system implementations, and third-party providers.
Develop risk-based audit programs and test procedures to assess IT general controls, application controls, and emerging technology risks using relevant frameworks.
Evaluate the design, implementation, and operating effectiveness of controls across ERP systems, research systems, cloud platforms, and critical infrastructure.
Prepare clear, concise audit reports and present actionable solutions to Management.
Resolve complex audit issues and escalate key risks and control gaps to senior leadership in a timely manner.
Ensure audit work meets professional standards with high-quality documentation and reporting.
Build effective working relationships with IT Services, cybersecurity teams, and administrative units

Audit Planning & Risk Assessment

Support the development and ongoing refinement of the risk-based internal audit plan with a focus on technology risks and digital transformation initiatives.
Conduct IT risk assessments in emerging risk areas such as Al, cloud computing, and cybersecurity, to inform audit priorities.
Provide insights into institutional risk exposures and control maturity across IT domains.

Audit Systems, Tools & Innovation

Support administration of our audit and compliance platforms (e.g., OpsAudit and CrossComply), ensuring effective configuration, data integrity, and usability.
Maintain and enhance audit tools and systems to support efficient audit execution and stakeholder reporting.
Collaborate with IT and business to ensure alignment between audit tools, governance frameworks, and institutional systems.

Data Analytics & Continuous Monitoring

Support the IT Audit Manager in leading the development and application of data analytics to enhance audit coverage, efficiency, and insight generation.
Analyze large datasets to identify trends, anomalies, and risks, supporting both individual audits and continuous monitoring initiatives.
Enable and mentor audit staff in the use of data analytics tools and techniques.

Business Intelligence & Reporting

Support the administration of the Internal Audit Power Bl environment, including governance, data models, and reporting assets.
Design and deliver dashboards and reports that provide meaningful insights into risk, audit results, and performance metrics.
Communicate findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences, including senior leadership.

Operational Contributions

Contribute to the continuous improvement of Internal Audit processes, methodologies, and templates.
Participate in departmental initiatives, special projects, and cross-functional work as required.

Qualifications / Requirements:

Education & Credentials

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Information Systems, Computer Science, Information Security, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
Professional certifications such as CISA, CIA, CISSP, and/or CPA is strongly preferred.

Experience

Minimum 3-6 years of relevant experience in IT audit, Internal Audit, cybersecurity, or related areas.
Experience executing IT audits, including testing general and application controls.
Experience working in complex or decentralized environments (public sector or higher education considered an asset).

Skills & Competencies

Deep knowledge of IIA Global Internal Audit Standards (GIAS) and IT control frameworks (e.g., COBIT, NIST, ISO 27001, ITIL).
Strong understanding of cybersecurity, data governance, privacy, and digital risk management.
Expertise in IT general controls, application controls, and system implementation reviews.
Advanced analytical and problem-solving skills with experience in data analytics tools (e.g., Power BI, ACL, Python).
Strong communication skills with the ability to translate technical risk into business impact.
Proven ability to build relationships and influence stakeholders in a decentralized environment.
Collaborative team player with strong interpersonal skills.

Application Deadline:
October 16, 2026

We would like to thank all applicants in advance for submitting their resumes. Please note, only those candidates chosen to continue on through the selection process will be contacted.

This position is classified in the Professional Career Band, Level 3
of the Management and Professional Staff Career Framework.

For a listing of all management and staff opportunities at the University of Calgary, view our Management and Staff Careers website
.

Founded in 1966, its 36,000 students experience an innovative learning environment, made rich by research, hands-on experiences and entrepreneurial thinking. jobs.title: Associate director, Financial Planning & Analysis
jobs.description:
Your impact begins here

As Associate Director, Financial Planning & Analysis, you will head the Financial Planning & Analysis team at Novo Canada. You will own the budgeting of ex-factory sales and costs, manage operating profit and guide how resources are allocated, giving the President, CFO and Executive Team the clarity to decide and act. Your work helps the affiliate reach its financial and strategic goals and keeps our products available to the people who rely on them.

What You’ll Bring

You combine strong financial expertise with the leadership to build a high-performing team.

You Will Also Bring

A bachelor/master’s degree in business administration, finance, business economics, accounting or auditing.
At least 5 years of experience in finance, with proven success in numbers-driven analysis, planning and reporting.
Experience presenting to senior management and executives, and the ability to explain quantitative analysis clearly.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, and a track record of planning, prioritising and following through while proactively managing risks.
A proven track record in complex, cross-affiliate project management.
An understanding of International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) and internal controls.
Proficiency in SAP, Business Warehouse and Excel.
In-depth understanding of the global budgeting process at Novo or a company of similar size.
A leadership style that builds trust, gives honest feedback, sets clear priorities and keeps things simple, especially through change.

What You’ll Do

You will lead the full financial planning cycle for Novo Canada and the commercial terms that connect our products to customers.

Your Work Will Help To

Lead, develop and plan the work of the Financial Planning & Analysis team, including hiring, succession, individual development plans and performance dialogue, and manage the team budget.
Oversee the affiliate P&L, including ex-factory sales, cost of goods sold and total operating costs, and own the total ex-factory sales forecast and targets.
Run the annual budget and rolling estimate processes, challenging submissions, ensuring compliance with corporate guidelines and anchoring approved targets across the business, while advising the President and CFO on resource allocation and supporting the Executive Team’s cost target.
Deliver monthly and quarterly reporting to management, the region and headquarters on sales, expenses and operating profit, flagging issues early and proposing corrective actions.
Own gross-to-net including rebate accruals under provincial Product Listing Agreements, and weekly sales performance reporting.
Lead priority initiatives for Financial Planning & Analysis and contribute to value-creation projects across Executive Team areas, and work with other affiliates to share best practices and keep planning simple and value-adding.

Who You’ll Work With

You will join Finance & Operations at Novo Canada as a member of the Finance & Operations Leadership Team. You will lead the Financial Planning & Analysis team, which you will help shape and grow.

Your closest partners will be the President, the CFO and the Executive Team. You will bring a financial perspective to the commercial teams, joining their management meetings, and support Line of Business colleagues with managing investments, month-end closing and training on financial processes.

You will also work with regional finance, headquarters, the Pricing Committee and colleagues in other affiliates, and directly with buyers at key wholesalers. These relationships let you turn numbers into clear, timely decisions.

What You Can Expect Here

You will take on a leadership role where your voice shapes decisions at executive level. The role gives you a broad view of the business, from budgets and operating profit to trade strategy, pricing and launches, and the opportunity to build new skills through cross-functional and cross-affiliate work.
You will be trusted to own your area and make decisions, with clear performance expectations and a culture that rewards results. You will also help your team thrive and grow through coaching, development plans and ongoing dialogue about performance and development.

What We Offer

At Novo, you'll join a global healthcare company with a unique culture and strong results. We offer continuous learning, career development, and benefits tailored to your life and career stage.

Salary:
For this role the Annual Base Salary ranges from $159,230.00 - $209,230.00

The placement in the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on your skills, competencies, knowledge and relevant experience match the position requirements

Incentives:
Based on the role's level and other factors, the salary package may include short-term (STI) and/or long-term (LTI) incentives.

Benefits:
The eligibility for specific benefits may vary based on the job and location

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

More information

This job posting is for an existing vacancy

Start now:
Your impact begins today. If you are ready to lead financial planning and trade strategy that helps Novo Canada reach its goals, apply for the Associate Director, Financial Planning & Analysis role by 16 October 2026
. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

Reporting to the IT Audit Manager, the Senior IT Auditor plays a key role in delivering the University's technology audit program. This position is responsible for executing and leading IT audit engagements and providing independent, objective assurance over the effectiveness of IT processes and controls.

Operating within a complex and decentralized academic environment, the Senior IT Auditor will work closely with business and IT stakeholders to identify risks and practical improvements that support organizational objectives. The successful candidate combines strong technical knowledge with business acumen to evaluate both technology and business risks, provide advisory services, and contribute to the continuous improvement of the organization's control environment.

Summary of Key Responsibilities
(job functions include but are not limited to):

Technology Audit Delivery (Primary Focus)

Lead and execute complex IT assurance engagements, from planning through reporting.
Identify and assess risks related to cybersecurity, privacy, business continuity, system implementations, and third-party providers.
Develop risk-based audit programs and test procedures to assess IT general controls, application controls, and emerging technology risks using relevant frameworks.
Evaluate the design, implementation, and operating effectiveness of controls across ERP systems, research systems, cloud platforms, and critical infrastructure.
Prepare clear, concise audit reports and present actionable solutions to Management.
Resolve complex audit issues and escalate key risks and control gaps to senior leadership in a timely manner.
Ensure audit work meets professional standards with high-quality documentation and reporting.
Build effective working relationships with IT Services, cybersecurity teams, and administrative units

Audit Planning & Risk Assessment

Support the development and ongoing refinement of the risk-based internal audit plan with a focus on technology risks and digital transformation initiatives.
Conduct IT risk assessments in emerging risk areas such as Al, cloud computing, and cybersecurity, to inform audit priorities.
Provide insights into institutional risk exposures and control maturity across IT domains.

Audit Systems, Tools & Innovation

Support administration of our audit and compliance platforms (e.g., OpsAudit and CrossComply), ensuring effective configuration, data integrity, and usability.
Maintain and enhance audit tools and systems to support efficient audit execution and stakeholder reporting.
Collaborate with IT and business to ensure alignment between audit tools, governance frameworks, and institutional systems.

Data Analytics & Continuous Monitoring

Support the IT Audit Manager in leading the development and application of data analytics to enhance audit coverage, efficiency, and insight generation.
Analyze large datasets to identify trends, anomalies, and risks, supporting both individual audits and continuous monitoring initiatives.
Enable and mentor audit staff in the use of data analytics tools and techniques.

Business Intelligence & Reporting

Support the administration of the Internal Audit Power Bl environment, including governance, data models, and reporting assets.
Design and deliver dashboards and reports that provide meaningful insights into risk, audit results, and performance metrics.
Communicate findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences, including senior leadership.

Operational Contributions

Contribute to the continuous improvement of Internal Audit processes, methodologies, and templates.
Participate in departmental initiatives, special projects, and cross-functional work as required.

Qualifications / Requirements:

Education & Credentials

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Information Systems, Computer Science, Information Security, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
Professional certifications such as CISA, CIA, CISSP, and/or CPA is strongly preferred.

Experience

Minimum 3-6 years of relevant experience in IT audit, Internal Audit, cybersecurity, or related areas.
Experience executing IT audits, including testing general and application controls.
Experience working in complex or decentralized environments (public sector or higher education considered an asset).

Skills & Competencies

Deep knowledge of IIA Global Internal Audit Standards (GIAS) and IT control frameworks (e.g., COBIT, NIST, ISO 27001, ITIL).
Strong understanding of cybersecurity, data governance, privacy, and digital risk management.
Expertise in IT general controls, application controls, and system implementation reviews.
Advanced analytical and problem-solving skills with experience in data analytics tools (e.g., Power BI, ACL, Python).
Strong communication skills with the ability to translate technical risk into business impact.
Proven ability to build relationships and influence stakeholders in a decentralized environment.
Collaborative team player with strong interpersonal skills.
